     THESE APPEALS ARE FILED UNDER SECTION 15T OF
THE SECURITIES AND EXCHANGE BOARD OF INDIA ACT,
1992 TO QUASH AND SET ASIDE ORDERS DATED 19TH
JUNE, 2023 AND 31ST JULY, 2023 PASSED BY THE WHOLE
TIME MEMBER AND ADJUDICATING OFFICER, SEBI.

     THESE APPEALS HAVING BEEN HEARD AND
RESERVED FOR ORDERS ON 30TH JUNE, 2025, COMING ON
FOR PRONOUNCEMENT OF ORDER THIS DAY, THE
TRIBUNAL MADE THE FOLLOWING:

                                   ORDER

Per: Ms. Meera Swarup, Technical Member Aggrieved by the two separate orders on same set of facts, one by the WTM1 and AO2, SEBI3, Appellant preferred the above captioned appeals. The same were heard together and are disposed off by this common order.

2. Appeal No. 771 of 2023 has been filed against the impugned order passed by the WTM dated 19TH June, 2023 whereby the Appellant has been directed to disgorge an 1 Whole Time Member 2 Adjudicating Officer 3 Securities and Exchange Board of India 3 amount of Rs.14,23,074/- along with interest at the rate of 4% per annum from 15TH April, 2013 till actual payment. The order also restrains the Appellant from accessing the securities market for a period of 6 months from the date of order and from dealing in shares of Wockhardt for period of 1 year from the date of the said WTM order for violation of Regulation 3(i) of PIT SEBI (Prohibition of Insider Trading) Regulations 1992 read with SEBI (Prohibition of Insider Trading) Regulations, 2015. In the said impugned order the Appellant is alleged to be an insider who traded in the shares of Wockhardt while in possession of UPSI4 during UPSI period. The UPSI period has been taken by SEBI as 22nd March, 2013 to 15th April, 2013.

3. Appeal 772 of 2023 has been filed against the impugned order passed by the AO imposing a penalty of Rs. 12 lakhs on the Appellant for violation of Regulation 3(i) of SEBI (Prohibition of Insider Trading) Regulations, 1992 read with SEBI (Prohibition of Insider Trading) Regulations, 2015 alleging the Appellant to be an insider and trading in the shares of Wockhardt while in possession of UPSI during the aforesaid UPSI period.

4. Brief facts of the case are that the Appellant was an erstwhile employee of Wockhardt Limited and was associated with the said company from April 2005 till April 2016. The Appellant during his association with Wockhardt had, from time to time, been allotted Employee Stock Options (ESOPS) which he had exercised. He eventually redeemed these shares by entering sales trades in the market at the then prevailing prices at the Stock exchanges. During his 4 Unpublished Price Sensitive Information 4 association with Wockhardt a total of 1,65,000 ESOPS were granted to the Appellant, which were exercised by him.

5. The Appellant at that time was responsible for product development and technology transfer of products and was also providing support to manufacturing for any clarification or data required by the USFDA (United States Food and Drug Administration). The USFDA conducted a routine inspection of Wockhardt's Waluj factory from 18th March, 2013 to 22nd March, 2013 with respect to data pertaining to abbreviated new drug application filed by Wockhardt with them and thereafter USFDA issued an adverse observation letter, i.e. Form 483 to Wockhardt, which is referred to as the "UPSI". It is not in dispute that on the same day i.e. 22nd March, 2013, US FDA had published the said Form 483 on its website and the rumors thereof started on 11th April, 2013 which were confirmed by press release on Wockhardt's website on 15th April, 2013, thus, leading to a fall in the price of scrip of Wockhardt by 15% within those 4 days. The appellant being an employee of Wockhardt is alleged to have access to the said UPSI.

6. The Appellant, in and around November 2014, received summons from SEBI's investigation Department whereby they sought certain information/documents with respect to Appellant's trades during the period January 2012 to July 2013. The Appellant vide its letter dated 12 th December, 2014 provided all the information/documents, which the SEBI had sought. Subsequent to this letter of the Appellant, SEBI made no communication with the Appellant in this regard.

5

7. However, SEBI issued a Show Cause Notice on 5th September, 2022 with regard to debarment and disgorgement under Sections 11B and 11(4) of the SEBI Act, 1992 and a Show Cause Notice on 15th September, 2022, with regard to penalty under Sections l5(G)(i), 15HA and 15HB of the SEBI Act, 1992 and 23E of SCRA, 1956. Upon request of the Appellant, inspection of documents was provided on 16th November, 2022. The Appellant thereafter filed his replies on 12th January, 2023 to the WTM-SCN and on 18th October, 2022, 27th January, 2023, 7th February, 2023 and 19th April, 2023 to the AO-SCN. Further, personal hearing on 17th January, 2023 was given before the WTM and on 19th April, 2023 before the Ld. AO. The WTM after perusing the relevant documents and on hearing the Appellant in detail, passed the disgorgement order on 19th June, 2023. Similarly, the AO after perusing the relevant documents and hearing the Appellant in detail passed the penalty order on 31st July, 2023.

8. We have heard Shri Deepak Dhane, learned Advocate for the appellant and Shri Pradeep Sancheti, learned Senior Advocate for the Respondent.

9. It was vehemently argued by the counsel for the Appellant that there is a long unexplained delay in initiation as well as completion of proceedings against the Appellant. The period of impugned trades pertains to the period 22 nd March, 2013 to 14th April, 2013, when the alleged trades were executed by the Appellant. Admittedly, the SCNs were issued after a lapse of more than 9 years on 5th September, 2022 and 15th September, 2022 and after 8 years of the issuance of the summons and, therefore, the said impugned orders should be quashed on this ground itself on account of 6 inordinate delay. On merits, the Appellant contended that Form - 483 is just an observation letter, which is issued in a routine manner for every pharmaceutical company after conclusion of on an inspection by USFDA. Form - 483 is issued on the last day of inspection and the Company is advised to take steps with respect to the said observations. Mere issuance of Form - 483 cannot be said to be information, which may affect the price of the shares of the Company. In most of the cases, upon complying with the observations, the matter stands resolved.

10. It is a matter of record that the prices between 16 th April, 2013 right upto middle of May 2013 were in the range of Rs. 1700 to Rs. 1930 which is completely contradictory to SEBI's case. Appellant contended that he has been regularly selling shares of Wockhardt since the year 2005 right upto 2017 in a routine manner and therefore the subject trades on 23rd, 25th and 28th March, 2013 were routine sales and said sales had nothing to do with the alleged UPSI in the nature of Form - 483.

11. The Senior Advocate for the SEBI submitted that issuance of Form - 483 to Wockhardt on 22nd March, 2013 was considered as a Price Sensitive Information ('PSI') in terms of Regulation 2(ha) of the PIT Regulations, 1992 as it was likely to materially affect the price of securities of the Company. The same was confirmed/announced by way of a Press Release on 15 April, 2013 by Wockhardt on its official website. Thus, period from 22nd March, 2013 to 15th April, 2013 is rightly considered as period of UPSI.

12. It is SEBI's Case that when the information relating to subject Form - 483 became public on April 15, 2013, share 7 prices had fallen, and therefore, this information was price sensitive in nature. During the investigation period, the Appellant worked for Wockhardt as President, Pharma Research, Global IP, QA/QC and Regulatory Affairs and had traded in the scrip of the Company during the UPSI period. The investigation further revealed that the Appellant who was also based out of the Waluj factory at the relevant time had sold 6841 shares of the Company during the UPSI period and had thereby avoided loss to the tune of Rs. 14,23,074/- (Rupees Fourteen Lakhs Twenty-Three Thousand Seventy-Four Only). In just five trading days, the scrip of Wockhardt saw a drastic price fall i.e. by 15.9%. The Appellant anticipating the loss, look the advantage of such crucial information and sought to sell his share in the market. Further, the defence of the Appellant that he had sold the said shares for payment of certain taxes and to pay for the consideration of shares acquired through exercise of ESOPs cannot be a justification for trading while in possession of UPSI and it is a clear violation of Regulation 3(i) of PIT Regulations, 1992.

13. On the contention of the appellant regarding inordinate delay in issuing the SCNs, the learned Senior Advocate for the Respondent stated that the Appellant has merely stated that the delay has severely prejudiced him, without pointing out any particular document or information which the Appellant could not retrieve due to the alleged delay in the mater, which has prejudiced his defense. Moreover, the fact that substantial amount of time has elapsed has been considered by the WTM while deciding on the period of debarment and interest on the amount of disgorgement and by the AO while deciding the amount of penalty. In support of the same, the SEBI has relied upon 8 Sudhir Gupta vs. State & Ors. (Delhi HC Judgment in Crl. M.C. No. 6620/2006) and the judgment of Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of V. K. Agarwal, Asst. Collector of Customs vs. Vasantraj Bhagwanji Bhatia & Ors. (1988 AIR 1106).

14. SEBI submitted that the Appellant is liable for the violation of clause 3.3 of Schedule 1 of Part A of PIT Regulations, 1992 read with Regulation 12(2) of PIT Regulations, 2015 as he was required to seek pre-clearance for trading in Wockhardt scrip when the total number of shares exceeded 4000 in a calendar month, as per the Company's Code of Conduct. However, Appellant sold 10,341 shares in one calendar month i.e. March, 2013 without taking any pre-clearance as he wrongly believed that pre-clearance for trades would be required only when the quantity in the year exceeded 40,000 shares.

15. The Respondent has adhered to the principles of natural Justice and has considered the Appellant's submissions and contentions presented both before the WTM and the AO and passed the impugned orders.

16. Having heard the learned counsel for the parties, we are of the opinion that the appeal is liable to be allowed on the short ground of inordinate delay in the initiation of the proceedings. From the impugned orders, we do not find any justification forwarded by the Respondent as to why it took so long to initiate and complete the proceeding. We note that the WTM in his order has only mentioned that the Appellant neither in his reply nor during the hearing could point out any document or information which he could not retrieve due to the delay in the matter. The WTM has given 9 no reason for SEBI to have delayed the matter for more than 8 years. The AO has only concluded that in view of the time taken to complete the investigation, there was no inordinate delay in the initiation of the proceedings. AO further states that there is no provision under the SEBI Act or its Regulations which prescribes a time limit for initiation of a show cause notice and, consequently held that there was no inordinate delay in the initiation of the proceedings.

17. In Ashlesh Gunvantbhai Shah vs. Sebi Appeal No. 169 of 2019 along with connected appeals decided on January 31, 2020, this Tribunal held:-

"12. Having considered the matter we are of the view that there has been an inordinate delay on the part of the respondent in initiating proceedings against the appellants for the alleged violations. The controversy in this regard is squarely covered by a decision of this Tribunal in Mr. Rakesh Kathotia & Ors. vs SEBI in Appeal No. 7 of 2016 decided by this Tribunal on May 27, 2019. The relevant paragraph is extracted herein below:-
"23. It is no doubt true that no period of limitation is prescribed in the Act or the Regulations for issuance of a show cause notice or for completion of the adjudication proceedings. The Supreme Court in Government of India vs. Citedal Fine Pharmaceuticals, Madras and Others, [AIR (1989) SC 1771] held that in the absence of any period of limitation, the authority is required to exercise its powers within a reasonable period. What would be the reasonable period would depend on the facts of each case and that no hard and fast rule can be laid down in this regard as the determination of this question would depend on the facts of each case. This proposition of law has been consistently reiterated by the Supreme Court in Bhavnagar University v. Palitana Sugar 10 Mill (2004) Vol.12 SCC 670, State of Punjab vs. Bhatinda District Coop. Milk P. Union Ltd (2007) Vol.11 SCC 363 and Joint Collector Ranga Reddy Dist. & Anr. vs. D. Narsing Rao & Ors. (2015) Vol. 3 SCC 695. The Supreme Court recently in the case of Adjudicating Officer, SEBI vs. Bhavesh Pabari (2019) SCC Online SC 294 held:
"There are judgments which hold that when the period of limitation is not prescribed, such power must be exercised within a reasonable time. What would be reasonable time, would depend upon the facts and circumstances of the case, nature of the default/statute, prejudice caused whether the third party rights had been created etc.
13. Similar view was again relied in Ashok Shivlal Rupani & Ors. vs. SEBI (Appeal No. 417 of 2018 along with other connected appeals decided on August 22, 2019) and again in Sanjay Jethalal Soni & Ors. vs. SEBI in Appeal No. 102 of 2019 and other connected appeals decided on November 14 2019.
14. We also find that in the case of Ashok Shivlal Rupani (supra) the period of investigation was January 4, 2010 to January 10, 2011 in the scrip of M/s. Oregon Commercial Ltd. and the show cause notice issued on November 20, 2017 which this Tribunal held that there was an inordinate delay. In the instant case, the same scrip was investigated for the same period and there is a delay of 7 years in issuing the show cause notice. To this extent, the facts are common. Further, Civil Appeal No. 8444 - 8445 of 2019 Securities and Exchange Board of India vs. Ashok Shivlal Rupani & Anr., etc. was dismissed by the Supreme Court on November 15, 2019 thus affirming the decision of this Tribunal.
15. In the light of the aforesaid, we are of the opinion that there has been an inordinate delay in the issuance of the show cause notice. Even 11 though there is no period of limitation prescribed in the Act and Regulations in the issuance of a show cause notice or for completion of the adjudication proceedings the authority is required to exercise its powers within a reasonable period as held recently in Adjudicating Officer, Securities and Exchange Board of India vs. Bhavesh Pabari (2019) SCC OnLine SC 294. In the instant case, we are of the opinion that the power to adjudicate has not been exercised within a reasonable period and therefore no penalty could be imposed."

18. In Sanjay Jethalal Soni and Ors. Vs. SEBI Appeal No. 102 of 2019 decided on November 14, 2019, this Tribunal held:-

"11. Having heard the learned counsel for the parties at some length we find that the respondent had investigated the scrips of Shree Global Tradefin Ltd. for the period March 1, 2009 to January 10, 2011 in September 2011. Pursuant thereto, a show cause notice dated April 20, 2012 was issued for the violation found during the investigated period March 1, 2009 to November 30, 2009. The respondents thereafter waited for another five years to issue a second show cause notice dated July 20, 2017 for the investigated period April 1, 2010 to January 10, 2011 which had been investigated in September 2011. We find that the respondents were aware of the alleged violation and thus there is no justification for waiting for more than five years to issue the second show cause notice dated July 20, 2017. In our view there is an inordinate delay in initiating the proceedings."

19. In Alps Motor Finance Ltd. vs. SEBI Appeal No. 620 of 2023 and connected appeals decided on 20th July, 2023 in similar circumstances the preferential allotment of shares was made between June 2013 to August 2013. The show cause notice was issued on 5th January, 2023. This Tribunal by its order dated 20th July, 2023 held 12 that there was an inordinate delay in the issuance of the show cause notice and, therefore, the order was set aside. The said decision is squarely applicable in the instant case.

20. Having examined the appeals in detail, we are of the opinion that there is an inordinate delay in the issuance of the show cause notice and proceedings. We note that the investigation period was from 7th January, 2012 to 7th August, 2013 and thereafter, the summons were issued in around November 2014 i.e. after more than 19 months from the date of trades in question. The Appellants had submitted necessary information/documents vide letter dated 12th December, 2014. SEBI took almost eight years to issue a show cause notices after the issuance of the summons. Both WTM and AO failed to give any explanation for this inordinate delay in their orders. There was no justification for issuance of the show cause notices at such a belated stage, which clearly shows lackadaisical approach of SEBI in dealing with this issue.

21. The contention of SEBI that the Appellant was not able to substantiate as to how any prejudice has been caused to him is not tenable as we note that the Appellant was only associated with Wockhardt until April 2016. After a substantial period of almost 6 years of non-association with the Wockhardt getting relevant documents/information with regards to the issue pertaining to the Form - 483 in 2012 would itself be a sufficient cause for prejudice caused to the Appellant. As a result, without going into the merits of the case, we are of the view that the impugned orders passed against the appellants cannot be sustained and are quashed. Hence, the following:-

13
ORDER i. Appeals allowed;
ii. The impugned orders passed against the appellants in Appeal Nos. 771 of 2023 and 772 of 2023 are quashed.
iii. The disgorgement / penalty amount deposited by the Appellant, under protest, may be refunded to the Appellant along with interest within six weeks from this order.
Pending interlocutory application(s), if any, stands disposed of. No costs.
Justice P.S. Dinesh Kumar Presiding Officer Ms. Meera Swarup Technical Member Dr. Dheeraj Bhatnagar Technical Member 06.08.2025 MADHUKAR Digitally signed by MADHUKAR BHALBAR msb BHALBAR Date: 2025.08.06 14:17:38 +05'30'
